draft.title: The Great Depression
card: In October 1929 share prices on the Wall Street stock exchange in New York collapsed. Many investors and banks lost money, and American banks and businesses cut back sharply.

The US had lent heavily to Europe, especially Germany, and US lenders now called in loans and stopped new ones. Countries also raised tariffs (taxes on imports) to protect local jobs, so world trade collapsed.
Firms that lost sales laid off workers. Unemployment soared in many countries, and by 1932 about one German worker in three had no job.
Many people lost faith in the governments in power. Some voters turned to extreme parties that promised work and change, such as the Nazis in Germany and the Communists.
draft.remember: The crash cut trade and jobs, and hardship pushed many voters towards extreme parties.

a.q: Why did the Wall Street crash of 1929 lead to unemployment in Germany?
opts: US lenders called in loans, and trade and industry shrank
Germany had to pay the United States a large tax on exports
Germany lost its colonies to the United States in 1929
German voters chose to leave their jobs to protest
a.why: The crash made US lenders call in loans, and trade and demand fell, so German firms cut jobs. The crash did not give the US any power to tax German exports or take its territory.
a.clue: Think about who had lent money to Germany.

b.q: In 1932 a town in Germany has one in three workers jobless. Which outcome fits best with the effects of the Depression?
opts: Voters there turn to parties that promise jobs and change
Voters there trust the governing parties more than before
Voters there stop voting because trade has recovered
Voters there back tariff cuts to help world trade grow
b.why: Hardship made many people lose faith in the governments in power, so some backed extreme parties that promised work. Trust in governments did not rise, and tariffs were being raised, not cut, as trade collapsed.
b.clue: Consider how people feel about the government when jobs vanish.

a.best: US lenders called in loans, and trade and industry shrank

b.best: Voters there turn to parties that promise jobs and change
